answer_1.quote: In this paper, we consider adversarial attacks on human-centric chatbots and dialogue systems...
answer_1.outputs: attack utterances, defender responses, toxic or non‑toxic generated texts

answer_2.quote: We report "attack effectiveness" by calculating the percentage of conversations in which the defender was provoked... The perplexity of the no attack case (unaltered DialoGPT conversations) is ∼39. This automatically confirms that our attacks are more fluent and natural...

answer_4.quote: We conduct human experiments in which we ask workers on Amazon's Mechanical Turk (AMT) to rate the conversations... AMT workers rated the generated attack's fluency, relevancy of the attack to previous utterances, and overall conversation coherency on a likert scale of 1 to 3 ... and also asked AMT workers to rate if the utterance after the attack is toxic or not.
answer_4.guideline: Workers rated fluency, relevancy, and coherency on a 1‑3 Likert scale and indicated whether the utterance was toxic.
